About Soracom

At Soracom, our mission is Making Things Happen, For a World That Works Together. We believe technologies such as connectivity, cloud and AI, have the power to transform industries, enable innovation, and help businesses solve real-world challenges. From startups launching their first connected product to global enterprises managing millions of devices, we empower our customers to bring their ideas to life.

With remote teams across Japan, the US, and Europe, Soracom continues to expand its global team to keep pace with the company's rapid growth. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and take pride in the diversity of our employees, valuing the unique experiences, perspectives, and expertise that people from different backgrounds bring to our business. We believe in Developing a Dream Team by hiring exceptional people, investing in their growth, and creating an environment where individuals and teams can do their best work.

The ability to develop groundbreaking technologies is one of our key assets, and our people make it happen. Come join Soracom and help create the transformative technology that enables our customers to engineer a better world.

About the Role

This is an ecosystem operating role with a leadership mandate, not a program management role with a team attached to it.

As Head of Partner Ecosystem reporting to the regional CEO, you will lead Soracom's Partner Success Leaders and Partner Development Leaders across the Americas, owning the full partner lifecycle from recruitment and onboarding through activation, revenue contribution, and compounding ecosystem growth. You will be accountable for the team's output and personally embedded in the highest-leverage partner relationships. You are a player-coach in the truest sense: you develop operators, and you are one.

The best partner ecosystems are built on partner quality, executive sponsorship, data visibility, and the deliberate use of levers like incentives, joint planning, and CRM integration. You know how to make those flywheels turn. You also know how to recognize when one is turning the wrong way, and how to intervene before a negative spiral takes hold.

This role is for someone on a trajectory toward Chief Ecosystem Officer or Chief Partnerships Officer, with the commercial instincts, operational rigor, and executive presence to eventually own this function at the company level. We are building that future here.

Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership and Operator Development. Lead, coach, and develop a team of Partner Success Leaders and Partner Development Leaders. Hold operators to outcome-based accountability rather than activity metrics, and set the standard by modeling that behavior yourself: tracking in the CRM, reporting on revenue and cycle time, owning a number.

Ecosystem Architecture. Design and continuously improve the partner program structure: tiers, incentives, rules of engagement, onboarding sequences, and partner health scoring. Prove the motion before scaling it.

Revenue Ownership. Own partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline targets for the Americas. Lead QBRs grounded in partner performance data. Prove measurable ecosystem contribution to the GTM motion.

GTM Orchestration. Define and hold the handoffs between Partner Development and Partner Success. Work in close, continuous partnership with the Head of Sales and Head of Marketing, co-owning pipeline targets, aligning on partner-influenced deal strategy, and establishing the joint planning and communication rhythm that keeps the field sales team equipped, informed, and actively engaged in partner-sourced opportunities. Represent the ecosystem in cross-functional planning, budget reviews, and strategic conversations.

Strategic Partner Ownership. Personally own a select set of top-tier partners, those where executive sponsorship, deal complexity, or strategic importance require your direct involvement.

Ecosystem Intelligence and AI Operations. Use AI tools to run a faster, more data-informed ecosystem: partner scoring, pipeline intelligence, enablement content generation, QBR prep, and competitive signal monitoring. Build AI fluency as a team capability.

Executive Visibility. Carry the ecosystem into rooms where it is not represented. Build executive-level relationships with key partners, speak for the Soracom partner ecosystem internally to senior leadership and externally at industry events, and translate ecosystem performance into C-suite language: revenue, market access, speed, and ROI.

Who You Are

A leader who stays close to the work. You have built and scaled partner teams without ever losing your hands-on instinct. You stay near the work because you want to be there, and your team can see it.

An operator before a relationship manager. You ask what a partner is supposed to produce before you ask how to keep them happy. The relationship is the vehicle, and the outcome is the destination. Your team knows this because you show them, not because you tell them.

A systems architect. You see the ecosystem as inputs, levers, and loops. You design programs the way engineers design products, with measurable outputs and feedback built in, and you fix upstream problems before adding downstream activity.

A builder comfortable with ambiguity. You thrive in fast-moving environments, make decisions with incomplete information, and are energized by the chance to build something that compounds.

Globally minded and culturally fluent. You are excited to work across time zones and cultures as part of a genuinely global team, and you bring the cross-cultural intelligence to build trust with partners in every geography.

An inclusive people leader. You build high-performing teams by creating clarity, trust, and accountability, and an environment where people can challenge ideas, grow, and do their best work.

Requirements

Key Requirements

  • At least 10 years of partner or ecosystem experience, including at least 3 years leading a partner team
  • Demonstrated player-coach profile: hands-on partner ownership alongside people leadership
  • Proven track record of partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue, carried against a quota, with the metrics to back it up
  • Experience designing or rebuilding partner programs: tiers, incentives, onboarding, partner health scoring
  • Cross-functional leadership across Sales, Marketing, Product, RevOps, and Finance
  • Demonstrated AI fluency as a daily operating practice
  • Ability to travel approximately 30%, including strategic partner meetings, team gatherings, and industry events

*We know great candidates don't always meet every qualification listed. If you're excited about this role and believe your experience could help us build a world-class partner ecosystem, we encourage you to apply — even if your background doesn't match every requirement or bonus qualification.

Bonus Points If…

  • You have experience with cellular or IoT connectivity solutions and services
  • You have built toward or operated at a VP or Chief Partnerships / Ecosystem Officer level
  • AWS Partner Network experience; understanding of cloud-era partner ecosystems required
  • You have hands-on experience with Salesforce CRM, PRM, or ecosystem intelligence platforms (Crossbeam, Tackle, or equivalent)
  • You have used AI to build team-wide partner operating workflows — not just personal productivity tools
  • You also speak Spanish
  • You live in a major metro area with easy access to air travel (e.g., Chicago, Atlanta, Minneapolis, New York, Seattle, Denver, Phoenix, Los Angeles)

Location

Fully remote work, based in the US

Benefits

    • Remote-first work environment for employees based in the United States
    • Flexible scheduling that supports productivity and work-life balance while accommodating customer needs and team collaboration
    • Access to modern tools, a dedicated technology budget, and leading AI platforms to help you innovate, learn, and do your best work
    • Opportunities for rapid learning, professional development, and career growth through exposure to complex, real-world customer challenges
    • Skills-based career progression, with advancement based on impact, contribution, and performance rather than tenure
    • Collaborative, globally distributed team environment with experienced and highly capable colleagues across the US, Europe, and Japan
    • Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental, and vision coverage

jobs.description:
ABOUT OLIPOP

At OLIPOP, we’re on a mission to positively impact consumer health at scale. And we’re doing it through something simple: soda. But not just any soda, a new kind of soda: one that’s delicious, refreshing, and actually good for you.

This mission is deeply personal for our CEO, Co-Founder, and Formulator, Ben Goodwin. Like many of us, Ben grew up consuming the Standard American Diet: lots of soda and processed foods that prioritized convenience over nutrition. But at 14, he took his health into his own hands. After making significant changes to his nutrition and exercise, he lost 50 pounds and saw a transformation in his energy, mood, and emotional clarity.

Those changes sparked a deep curiosity about the connection between nutrition and health. Ben became a relentless student of the gut microbiome and the ways it supports overall wellness. The more he discovered, the more passionate he became about finding credible, science-backed ways to make consumer health accessible to everyone.

The mission was clear. The vehicle? Less so. After exploring the possibilities, Ben landed on an unexpected yet familiar choice: soda. It was something he loved as a kid, and he knew millions shared that same nostalgia. But this wouldn’t be just any soda. With most Americans falling short on daily fiber, Ben set out to create a version with more fiber and less sugar, one that was perfectly balanced. The result? A deliciously refreshing soda with 6 to 9 grams of fiber and 2 to 5 grams of sugar, delivering science-backed benefits without sacrificing the classic taste people crave.

In 2018, the first OLIPOP cans hit the shelves, bringing Ben’s vision to life with a functional soda that anyone could enjoy. And by reimagining soda, we’re also reshaping culture. That means creating products that support health for all and building a business grounded in humanistic values: empathy, integrity, and a belief in better for everyone. From the ingredients we source to the culture we foster, we’re committed to proving that business (and beverage!) can be a force for good, and that soda has the power to bring people together.

So join us, and let’s write a new American soda story together. One we can all feel good about. One OLIPOP at a time.

We’re looking for a Consumer Insights Manager to lead the voice of the consumer at OLIPOP. This person will own the development and execution of consumer learning plans that inform key business areas like marketing campaigns, new product development, creative direction, and strategic planning, and will mentor colleagues on translating insights into action. They’ll partner closely with internal teams and external research vendors, serving as a trusted advisor on insight-led decisions that drive both short-term performance and long-term brand growth. This role is a great fit for someone with deep functional expertise who’s curious, collaborative, and passionate about extending our insights capabilities across the organization.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
● Champion a consumer-first mindset across the marketing team and broader organization, mentoring colleagues on applying insights to strategic decisions
● Lead cross-functional and agency partnerships to embed the consumer perspective into briefs, business cases, and sales materials, advising stakeholders on insight-led tradeoffs
● Lead the design and execution of research projects that inform marketing and innovation decisions (e.g., concept testing, creative testing, sensory testing, etc.),
developing specialized expertise across methodologies
● Own vendor relationships and day-to-day project management, from design to reporting, ensuring findings are translated into clear, actionable recommendations
● Drive internal reporting and presentations that track brand KPIs, such as household penetration, brand awareness, and campaign performance, proactively surfacing trends and implications for leadership
● Build and evolve OLIPOP’s consumer knowledge, research tools, and insights capabilities, serving as a resource and mentor to colleagues across functions
● Monitor industry trends, cultural shifts, and emerging consumer behaviors, translating them into recommendations that shape brand strategy and innovation

REQUIREMENTS:
● 8+ years of experience in consumer insights, market research, or related roles, with demonstrated depth in a specialized research area (CPG experience preferred; beverage a plus)
● Highly collaborative, curious, and comfortable operating independently in a fast-paced, agile environment
● Advanced knowledge of both qualitative and quantitative research methods, with experience introducing new approaches to the function
● Strong organizational and project management skills – able to independently manage multiple complex projects and mentor others in prioritization
● Strong analytical skills – makes complex information simple and compelling for audiences at all levels, including senior leadership
● Experience writing and designing surveys to answer business questions, and comfortable advising others on research design
● Strategic thinker who connects consumer learning to business implications and influences functional strategy
● Proficiency with marketing mix modelling and DIY research tools
● Working knowledge of syndicated tools like Nielsen, SPINS, or Numerator preferred
● Track record of leading high-priority projects independently and mentoring or advising

Reports to: Director of Consumer Insights

Compensation: $115k-$135k base plus bonus

HOW WE WORK

We may be fully remote, but we’re anything but disconnected. OLIPOP has grown from a few passionate people around a table to a nationwide team, and we’ve done it without losing our collaborative spirit or sense of purpose.

Connection here is intentional. From cross-functional projects and IRL offsites to thoughtful Slack threads and spontaneous gifs, we make the effort to stay close, even across time zones. Sure, we move quickly, but we lead with trust, transparency, and a shared commitment to doing work that matters.

We value thoughtful debate. We give feedback with care and receive it with curiosity, knowing that real growth, both personal and collective, comes from listening as much as leading. Because at OLIPOP, it’s not just about getting things done. It’s about growing together, staying true to what matters, and building something with lasting impact.

WHAT WE VALUE

At OLIPOP, our values aren’t just posters on a wall. They shape how we show up: for each other, for our customers, and for the mission we’re chasing together.

  • Mission Connectivity: Everything we do ladders up to our shared goal: supporting human health. Whether launching a new flavor or conducting clinical research, the mission stays front and center.
  • Indomitable Spirit: When things get messy, we get inventive. We stay curious, adapt quickly, and find the path forward, most likely with a dedicated Slack thread and a beautifully overbuilt deck.
  • Lead at Every Level: Leadership isn’t about titles, it’s about ownership. We speak up, follow through, and lift each other up. If you’ve got ideas and initiative, you’ve got influence.
  • Courageous Humility: We’re confident in what we bring and curious about what we don’t know (yet). We give feedback with care, take it with grace, and know that real growth takes both.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Success at OLIPOP doesn’t come from checking boxes; it comes from living our values, staying curious, and finding energy in both the pace and the purpose. We’re building something big, and we’re looking for people who:

  • Think big, move fast, and take thoughtful risks
  • Thrive in a high-performance, feedback-rich environment
  • Value real human connection and honest collaboration
  • Are fired up by building something new, and making it better every day

Startup life at OLIPOP is equally fun and fast-paced. If you’re energized by a dynamic environment, eager to grow, and excited to help shape something meaningful from the inside out, OLIPOP is a one-of-a-kind ride.

This is an adaptive marketing role by design; Nymbus’s marketing team is nimble, our strategy shifts as we learn, and this person needs to move fluidly across channels rather than defend a single lane. Reporting to the Chief Strategy & Marketing Officer, you’ll also manage our Events Manager, since peer conferences and roundtables are one of the highest-trust channels we have.

OBJECTIVES OF THE ROLE

  • Build and run a regular analyst and consultant briefing cadence with the firm’s bank and credit union leadership and key decision-makers consult with before a vendor decision.
  • Direct external communications and industry press relations, ensuring Nymbus is credibly positioned in the specific trade publications that influence our target buyers.
  • Build a named-account marketing engine tied directly to Sales’ target list, reinforced by customer and peer advocacy and a clear product narrative.
  • Translate our modern banking platform capability in partnership with Product, ensuring comfort in product marketing efforts and acting as an advocate for how our products are positioned to the market through focused campaigns.
  • Establish and oversee a marketing technology architecture tailored to a high-value, relationship-centric, named-account lead generation strategy.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS/RESPONSIBILITIES:

Analyst & Consultant Relations

  • Own relationships with the analysts and consultants bank and credit union boards actually consult before a vendor decision.
  • Build and run a regular briefing cadence; prepare executive briefing and marketing materials with the CSMO and CEO.
  • Lead industry rankings, evaluations, and award submissions as a standing quarterly priority, not an ad hoc task.
  • Track and report on how analyst sentiment and coverage evolve as a leading indicator for the business.
  • Regularly audit marketing content for accuracy and relevance, and close content gaps, since outdated or inaccurate material in front of an analyst or a bank board is a credibility risk, not just a cleanup task.

PR, Communications & Industry Press

  • Own external communications strategy, with a focus on the trade press our buyers actually read.
  • Draft press releases, executive communications, and customer announcements.
  • Build direct relationships with the reporters and editors who cover bank/CU technology, not just distribute releases.
  • Collaborate with the Product team to define the product marketing narrative and competitive landscape for our modern banking platform, ensuring industry press accurately reflects Nymbus’ market position.
  • Support crisis communications when necessary

Account-Based & Named-Account Marketing

  • Build and run marketing programs and campaigns against Nymbus's named target list.
  • Maintain working knowledge of a meaningful share of target accounts by name and context.
  • Partner with Sales to identify what a specific target account's CEO or board needs to see or hear to move forward, and orchestrate it: a customer reference, an analyst mention, a peer introduction, a piece of content.
  • Collaboration with Client Partnership and Sales to build reference and advocacy programs that let prospects hear directly from peers already using Nymbus, and support peer roundtables, customer councils, and reference calls.
  • Design pre- and post-event campaign activations for peer conferences and roundtables that turns relationship touchpoints into named-account progress.

Marketing Operations & Team Leadership

  • Own day-to-day management of a marketing budget, with CSMO sign-off above an agreed threshold.
  • Coordinate agency and freelance partners.
  • Select, build, and maintain the marketing technology stack (CRM integration, ABM tooling, email/communications systems) appropriate to a named-account model, rather than defaulting to tools built for high-volume demand generation.
  • Track, measure, and report on marketing performance across all channels and initiatives, continuously refining tactics based on what matters in this model: analyst sentiment, named-account engagement, press coverage quality, and pipeline influence.
  • Lead and develop the Events Manager; ensure conferences, roundtables, and peer events are run as trust-building tools, not just logistics.
  • Improve marketing workflows and operating rhythms as the team grows.

AI-Driven Innovation

  • Integrate AI tools actively into strategic planning and daily workflow: market research, audience insights, creative testing, performance analysis, and competitive intelligence.
  • Champion new platform capabilities and automation opportunities that create strategic advantage for Nymbus Marketing.
  • Share learnings and continuously raise the bar for how the team uses AI to think faster, plan smarter, and deliver more.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 5 to 8 years of B2B marketing experience in a regulated, relationship-driven, or long-sales-cycle market: fintech, banking technology, enterprise SaaS to executive buyers, insurance, or similar; direct banking/credit union experience is a strong plus but not required.
  • Demonstrated ownership of analyst relations and/or industry press relationships, not just supporting them.
  • Account-based marketing experience against a defined, named target list, as opposed to persona-based segmentation at scale.
  • Comfort operating as a generalist, willing to shift focus across functions as strategy requires, rather than defending a single lane.
  • Strong executive communication skills, comfortable drafting for an executive audience.
  • Comfortable selecting and standing up marketing technology (CRM, ABM, email/communications tools) from scratch or reconfiguring an existing stack is a plus.
  • Cross-functional fluency working with Sales, Product, and Executive Leadership.
  • Experience marketing to bank or credit union executives, or another risk-averse, board-governed buyer, is a plus.
  • Familiarity with AI/agentic tools for content and marketing production is a plus.
  • Prior experience managing at least one direct report is a plus

SALARY & BENEFITS:

  • Annual Cash Bonus and Equity Options commensurate with the role level and experience
  • 100% Remote
  • 401(k) plan
  • Insurance - Health, Dental and Vision

jobs.description:
12twenty is the leading platform for employers to connect with elite early career professionals. Our community includes millions of students, recent graduates, and alumni from top business schools, law schools, and universities around the world. We take pride connecting our community of candidates with recruiters from top companies across industries. Come join our fast growing organization!

At 12twenty, we believe great content does more than fill a calendar. Great content builds trust, shapes markets, and drives growth.

We’re looking for a hands-on content marketer with exceptional writing skills who can transform data, customer insights, and industry trends into thought leadership that people genuinely want to read and share.

This role owns the editorial engine behind our marketing efforts. You’ll create compelling content, manage our editorial calendar, and ensure every piece of content supports our brand, demand generation, search visibility, and customer education goals.

Our messaging strategy is established. Your role is to bring it to life through outstanding storytelling, thoughtful execution, and an unwavering commitment to quality.

If you’re energized by turning research into reports, webinars into campaigns, and data into stories that move people to action, we’d love to meet you.

Content Strategy & Editorial Leadership

Content Creation & Thought Leadership

Campaigns & Demand Generation

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role isn’t measured by how much content you publish. It’s measured by the impact your content creates.

Funnel Leasing Inc. is hiring for a Senior Product Manager, AI. As the Senior Product Manager, AI, you will own the strategy, roadmap, requirements, and cross-functional execution of AI-powered experiences and platform capabilities across Funnel.

You will be tasked with actively translating customer and business problems into scalable AI systems, agentic workflows, and shared platform capabilities across product lines.

​​You’ll partner closely with Engineering, Design, Strategy, Customer Success, Implementation, Support, Finance/Operations, and external AI partners to take AI capabilities from concept through production. You’ll help define how we build, evaluate, and continuously improve AI agents and workflows, ensuring they are reliable, intuitive, and scalable while delivering measurable and sustained value to our customers and business.

This role is ideal for a product manager or technical product manager who is comfortable operating at the intersection of AI, product, and engineering. You should be technically fluent enough to understand AI architectures and technical proposals, ask effective implementation questions, evaluate tradeoffs, and translate complex technical concepts into clear product requirements and decisions. You should be comfortable navigating the ambiguity and non-deterministic nature of AI while bringing structure, rigor, and strong product judgment to how we build platform capabilities used across Funnel’s AI products. The salary range for this role is $155,000 - $195,000 per year.

Why Funnel?

We are a 'work from anywhere' in the U.S. SaaS company that centers our services on the renter experience. We develop amazing software that has revolutionized the #proptech industry. Who is Funnel Leasing?

Have you ever rented an apartment and wished the process could be better? At Funnel we do too. We know we need to make the process of renting an apartment as easy as purchasing socks on Amazon. Click here to learn more about Funnel and our innovative team members across the country.

The Senior Product Manager, AI essential roles and responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

  • Collaborate with our AI Features team and other Funnel Product Teams to design and implement AI-driven capabilities that power user experiences related to admins, renters, and leasing agents

  • Identify opportunities to simplify and standardize AI systems and agent behaviors, strengthen guardrails, reduce failure modes and escalations, and ensure issues can be efficiently detected, triaged, and resolved.

  • Performs other duties as assigned and modified at manager's discretion
  • Create a culture of continuous improvement and learning
  • Foster collaboration within team and across the company
  • Performs other duties as assigned and modified at manager's discretion
  • Travel: <5%

Education, Work Experience, and Certifications

  • 5+ years experience as a Product Manager, ideally with ownership of AI agents or AI-powered products
  • Direct experience building or managing AI agents that operate across conversational channels such as voice, chat, SMS, and email.
  • B2B SaaS experience using and understanding the capabilities of frontier LLMs (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.).
  • Ability to design, test, and refine prompts that clearly define AI behavior, context, constraints, and expected outcomes.
  • Strong understanding of large language models (LLMs), natural language processing (NLP), and the core concepts behind modern conversational and agentic AI systems.
  • Understanding of AI context and knowledge retrieval approaches, including Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Context-Augmented Generation (CAG), agentic retrieval, embeddings, and vector databases.
  • Strong ability to break down complex AI systems, agent behaviors, and platform capabilities into clear product requirements and pragmatic, phased delivery plans.

jobs.title: B2B Proposal Storyteller & Writer
jobs.excerpt: The connected device category is in one of its most consequential moments in years — and Assurant Global Connected Living is helping shape what comes next.
jobs.description:
The connected device category is in one of its most consequential moments in years — and Assurant Global Connected Living is helping shape what comes next.

We partner with many of the world's leading brands, supporting millions of customers across connected devices, homes, automobiles, and commercial equipment. Our purpose is simple: help people thrive in a connected world. As mobile, retail, OEM, and smart home ecosystems converge, customer experience, lifecycle economics, and brand trust are colliding in real time — and every proposal we win is a chance to prove what Assurant can do.

That's where you come in. We're looking for a B2B Proposal Storyteller & Writer who can find the through-line in complex business and technical information, ground it in customer, market, and competitive insight, and translate it into a data-backed, compelling business narrative that gives Assurant a clear “right to win.” This is a role for a writer who is strategic, rigorous, curious, and energized by work that directly shapes how Assurant competes and wins.

What makes you successful

  • You think critically and lead with business acumen. You don't just capture information — you interrogate it, find the insight others miss, and connect it to what actually moves a deal or a client relationship forward.

  • You build narratives on insight and evidence. You draw on customer, market, and competitive insight — and Assurant's proprietary data — to shape a differentiated point of view and a credible right-to-win, not just a well-written response.

  • You're a bold storyteller. You have a point of view, you're willing to make a confident recommendation, and you can turn complex, technical material into a narrative that's persuasive and impossible to ignore.

  • You build relationships across the organization. You lead with high EQ, read the room, and earn trust with Sales, Product, Legal, and SMEs — so people want to bring you their best thinking.

  • You're collaborative without losing your edge. You balance diverse perspectives and healthy debate, then synthesize them into one clear, differentiated position.

  • You bring rigor to the craft. Attention to detail, deadline discipline, and version-control instincts are second nature — because in this role, precision is part of the persuasion.

What will be my duties and responsibilities in this role?

Shape strategic, right-to-win narratives

  • Find the through-line in complex business and technical information and translate it into a clear, compelling narrative that positions Assurant as the best partner to win with — not just a viable option.

  • Help shape differentiated “right-to-win” narratives, win themes, and positioning tailored to each prospect's business, buyer personas, and decision dynamics.

  • Identify and codify Assurant's differentiators (current and emerging) and ensure they show up consistently across proposals, pitches, and live conversations.

  • Develop tailored storytelling frameworks — such as points of view, use-case narratives, and experience-led concepts — that show how Assurant unlocks incremental value, not just coverage.

Ground narratives in insight and data

  • Leverage customer, market, and competitive insight — along with Assurant's proprietary data — to sharpen storytelling and strengthen our right-to-win.

  • Translate insight into proof points, case studies, and evidence that make each narrative credible and hard to argue with.

  • Build and continuously improve a reusable library of win frameworks, proof points, and case studies that can be adapted quickly to account-specific needs without becoming generic.

Collaborate across the business to build winning content

  • Partner closely with Sales, Product, Legal, Account Management, Operations, and subject matter experts to align strategy, proof points, and delivery realities into one cohesive narrative.

  • Lead with high EQ to gather diverse inputs, balance healthy debate, and synthesize competing perspectives into a single, differentiated position.

  • Work with SMEs to ensure their ideas and vision are captured and expressed appropriately in client-facing content.

Author persuasive proposals & RFP responses

  • Review complex and detailed RFPs and work with the larger team to formulate the appropriate response “plan of attack.”

  • Contribute to and socialize RFP briefs that guide responses, key messages, and differentiators.

  • Translate complex products, services, technical capabilities, and detailed RFP line items into clear, concise, persuasive client-friendly messaging that sharpens our responses.

  • Respond to RFP questions with compelling, well-positioned answers that support technical knowledge and differentiation.

  • Develop high-impact sales materials — pitch decks, one-pagers, battlecards, cover letters, and executive summaries — that synthesize technical RFP responses into a compelling, high-level narrative supporting Assurant's win strategies.

  • Tailor content to specific industries, client segments, and buyer personas to increase relevance and conversion.

Continuously optimize sales-enablement content

  • Continuously improve a centralized content library of reusable responses, case studies, and proof points.

  • Create supporting content that may take the form of long- and short-form website content, ad copy, video scripts, associate talking points, and sales materials.

Coordinate feedback and manage versions

  • In conjunction with the proposal coordinator, manage feedback, revisions, and document versions in a fast-paced team environment.

  • Edit and revise written content based on feedback and business requirements.

What are the requirements needed for this position?

  • A minimum of 3 years of experience in B2B content strategy, proposal writing, sales enablement, marketing communications, or a related field; experience in consumer electronics, mobile, retail, or technology industries is preferred.

  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Advertising, Business Administration, Communications, Journalism, or a related field preferred.

  • Proven writing and storytelling skills, with the ability to turn complex business and technical information into clear, persuasive, insight-driven narratives for executive, partner, and customer audiences.

  • Experience shaping win themes, differentiators, and right-to-win positioning — using customer, market, or competitive insight and data to strengthen the story.

  • Experience developing proposals, RFP responses, presentations, sales collateral, case studies, thought leadership, and other customer-facing content.

  • Strong collaboration skills with the ability to partner across Sales, Product, Marketing, Legal, and subject matter experts to create winning content.

  • Self-motivated and adaptable, with a creative problem-solving mindset and openness to feedback and continuous improvement.

  • Highly organized with strong attention to detail, project management skills, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

What other skills / experience would be helpful to have?

  • Familiarity with account-based marketing (ABM), complex B2B sales cycles, and partnering closely with Sales and Account Management on live pursuits.

  • Experience creating content and narratives specifically designed to support RFPs, executive meetings, and live deal pursuits.

  • Comfort using insight and analytics to inform storytelling (e.g., customer research, competitive intelligence, sales-enablement or analytics tools).

  • Technical fluency; comfortable using standard web-based tools typical of remote work environments.

  • Understands the balance between “perfection” and “flawed-but-adequate,” and knows how and when to prioritize one over the other.

jobs.excerpt: Jeeves is a groundbreaking financial operating system built for global businesses that provides corporate cards, cross-border payments, and spend management software within one unified platform.
jobs.description:
Jeeves is a groundbreaking financial operating system built for global businesses that provides corporate cards, cross-border payments, and spend management software within one unified platform. The company operates across 20+ countries including Brazil, Canada, Colombia, Mexico, the United Kingdom, across Europe, and the United States, and serves over 5,000 clients ranging from venture-backed startups to SMBs around the world. With a mission to empower businesses with more efficient and cost-effective financial solutions worldwide, Jeeves combines cutting-edge financial technology with exceptional team expertise to transform the business financial landscape. Jeeves has been recognized as one of The Information's 50 Most Promising Startups in 2023, as well as a Y Combinator Top Company 2021-2023 and won “Fintech of the Year" at the European Fintech Awards.
Since graduating from Y Combinator in 2020, Jeeves has successfully raised over $380 million and is backed by top world-class investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator, CRV, Tencent, Stanford University, Clocktower Ventures, and founders of more than 15 unicorns including David Velez (Nubank), Carlos Garcia (Kavak) and Sebastián Mejía (Rappi).

You'll own Jeeves' stablecoin and digital asset strategy—defining how blockchain rails transform cross-border payments, treasury management, and settlement for global businesses. This role requires someone who is crypto-obsessed and deeply familiar with the stablecoin ecosystem: issuance and reserve models, on/off-ramp mechanics, fiat rail interoperability, and institutional adoption trends. We want someone who has built stablecoin or crypto payment products at a stablecoin issuer, crypto exchange, cross-border payment platform, or fintech building on blockchain rails.

Location: This role is based out of United States, and is a full-time remote position.

What You'll Do

    Stablecoin Product Strategy

    • Own the stablecoin product roadmap: which rails to build on, which stablecoins to support, and how they integrate into payments and treasury workflows

    • Build institutional-grade infrastructure that abstracts blockchain complexity while preserving speed and cost advantages for end users

    • Drive the full product lifecycle from ideation through launch, collaborating with engineering, design, legal, compliance, and commercial teams

      • Cross-Border Payments & Treasury

      • Build products that let businesses send, receive, convert, and hold stablecoins alongside fiat across USD, EUR, BRL, MXN, and local currency corridors

      • Design seamless on/off-ramp flows that feel as simple as traditional banking, even for users who have never touched crypto

      • Ensure interoperability with fiat rails (ACH, Fedwire, SWIFT, SEPA, PIX, SPEI) so stablecoins become a natural extension of existing payment infrastructure

        • Compliance, Risk & Custody

        • Navigate US state licensing, MiCA, and LatAm crypto regulations to ship compliant products in every market we serve

        • Embed AML/KYC, Travel Rule, and transaction monitoring requirements into the product from day one

        • Evaluate wallet infrastructure, custodians, and key management solutions that meet institutional-grade security standards

          • Partnerships & Go-to-Market

          • Evaluate and manage partnerships with stablecoin issuers, liquidity providers, custodians, and banking partners

          • Enable Sales and Customer Success to position stablecoin products and close deals with CFOs and treasury teams

          • Ship, measure, and iterate—track adoption metrics and ruthlessly prioritize based on data and business impact

What We're Looking For:

    Required

    • 4+ years in product management at a stablecoin infrastructure provider, crypto exchange, cross-border payments company, or fintech building on blockchain rails

    • Deep stablecoin expertise: issuance and redemption mechanics, reserve models, on-chain settlement, ecosystem dynamics, and how stablecoins interact with treasury flows and FX

    • Strong understanding of fiat rails: ACH, wires, RTP, SWIFT, SEPA, PIX, SPEI—and how reconciliation, settlement timing, and fiat conversions work alongside stablecoin flows

    • Blockchain infrastructure literacy: EVM chains, Solana, Layer 2s, wallet architecture, key management, and custody. Able to converse with engineers on API docs and system design

    • Regulatory fluency: AML/KYC frameworks, Travel Rule, MiCA, US state-by-state licensing, and how compliance requirements vary by jurisdiction

    • Analytical rigor: comfortable with SQL, dashboards, and building data-driven business cases

    • Exceptional communication: can write strategy memos and product specs that align cross-functional stakeholders

      • Strongly Preferred

      • Track record of owning complex, regulated financial products from concept through production at scale

      • Relationships in the stablecoin ecosystem—issuers, custodians, liquidity providers, or regulators

      • Experience with multi-market products serving LatAm, US, and/or European customers

      • Familiarity with developer platforms, API design, and ecosystem-driven products

      • Background in traditional payments or banking

Why This Role Matters:

    Cross-border payments move $150+ trillion annually through slow, expensive, opaque systems. Stablecoins are the most promising technology to fix this—but most stablecoin products today are built for crypto-native users, not the finance teams at global businesses who move billions daily. At Jeeves, you'll bridge that gap and shape how thousands of global businesses adopt stablecoin-powered finance.

jobs.title: Associate Human Resource Director
jobs.excerpt: What We Can Achieve Together: As a key member of the Western United States and Canada (WUSCAN) HR team, the Associate Human Resource Director (AHRD) builds strategic partnerships with leaders and HR team members and collaborates across multiple Business Units to implement human-centered and impactful HR initiatives that support The Nature Conservancy’s mission, values and organizational goals.
jobs.description:
What We Can Achieve Together:

As a key member of the Western United States and Canada (WUSCAN) HR team, the Associate Human Resource Director (AHRD) builds strategic partnerships with leaders and HR team members and collaborates across multiple Business Units to implement human-centered and impactful HR initiatives that support The Nature Conservancy’s mission, values and organizational goals. This role is instrumental in fostering an inclusive, high-performing, and equitable culture across the WUSCAN Division. The AHRD leads service delivery and strategic direction in the following human resource functions: employee relations, compensation, talent management, benefits, payroll, staff development and training, organizational development, performance management and recruiting for Canada and the United States. Reporting to the HR Director, the AHRD will manage a team of HR professionals located in multiple locations.

We’re Looking for You:

Are you looking for work you can believe in? At TNC we strive to embody a philosophy of Work that You Can Believe in where you can feel like you are making a difference every day. We’re looking for someone with strong experience in leading a geographically dispersed HR team. The ideal candidate develops business partnerships with senior leaders to establish and implement strategic HR direction to meet TNC's organizational goals and conservation mission. The AHRD works closely with all HR functions to integrate services and deliver timely support to business units. The AHRD also plays a leadership role implementing People strategies in support of ongoing operational improvements and to foster an open, inclusive, transparent, and equitable organizational culture. They will partner with other members of the WUSCAN HR team and People Team to collaboratively share responsibility for designing, developing and implementing innovative People practices aligned with TNC values, strategies and goals. They are experts in Canadian employment law and HR practices and are accountable for delivering relevant support and counsel for the full employee lifecycle in assigned Business Units that are geographically dispersed across Canada and the Western United States. They implement these People Team initiatives to ensure consistency in support of a global, decentralized and geographically dispersed enterprise. This role will supervise a small team of HR professionals supporting WUSCAN and leading the optimization of a new HR operating model in service of the business units. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the ongoing mission of conservation by directing and shaping the work of our divisional HR team!

We currently have one vacancy for an Associate HR Director.

Responsibilities & Scope:

  • Strategic HR Partnership and Consultation

    • Serve as a primary liaison between the People Team and Business Unit leaders to align HR priorities with business objectives and deliver consistent, high-quality HR practices.

    • Provide strategic counsel on organizational design, workforce planning, operational efficiencies, job creation or elimination, and resource optimization.

    • Advise managers on TNC policy and SOPs, HR processes, employment law and policy requirements, employee engagement, and effective management practices.

  • Employee Relations and Performance Management

    • Promote positive employee relations by facilitating conflict resolution, conducting investigations, and recommending remedies aligned with Conservancy policies, SOPs, competencies, and values.

    • Coach managers and staff on goal setting, timely feedback, continuous development, and high-performance practices.

    • Advise on complex performance management, employee relations, and separations, including voluntary and involuntary terminations, in partnership with HR Legal and senior HR staff as appropriate.

  • Compensation, Equity, and Talent Practices

    • Support job design, job description development, salary guidance, recruitment and offer terms development.

    • Lead team in conducting the annual pay equity analysis and supporting equitable promotion, compensation, and talent decisions.

    • Develop and implement HR programs and strategic initiatives, including talent reviews, succession planning, performance processes and recognition practices.

  • Learning, Development, and HR Service Delivery

    • Assess learning needs, deliver or coordinate HR-related training, build hiring manager capability, and support HR team members and liaisons in managing administrative HR functions.

    • Develop and implement HR standards and client service practices that strengthen consistency, accountability, and support across Business Units.

    • Lead or participate in cross-functional project teams to advance organizational priorities.

  • Team Leadership

    • Supervise a small HR team dedicated to providing exceptional service and support to geographically dispersed business units in Canada and the Western United States.

    • Provide coaching and development opportunities to grow team’s HR expertise and consistency of delivery.

    • Contribute to a culture of psychological safety, innovation, and results orientation.

What You’ll Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 8 years HR related experience supporting 300+ employee client groups in a global, matrixed, complex environment, or equivalent combination.

  • Experience developing and leading multiple HR-related projects and implementing strategic HR programs.

  • Experience supporting employees in both Canada and the United States with demonstrated knowledge of Federal and Provincial employment law including FLSA, ESA, and other related standards.

  • Experience managing the administration, progress, and maintenance of human resource functions in both Canada and the United States, for one or more of the following: employee relations, compensation and performance management, benefits, payroll, staff development/training, organizational development, and recruiting.

  • Experience working with senior managers to root cause HR issues and design, develop and implement HR strategies and initiatives.

  • Experience managing complex employee relations, facilitating and leading crucial conversations, and building effective consultative relationships.

  • Experience supervising HR teams of 2 or more employees, setting work priorities, establishing employee objectives/expectations and driving accountability across the team’s portfolio of work.

  • Experience managing confidential employee matters and employee data in adherence to local laws and data privacy best practices.

  • Experience using MS Office software with experience in constructing and producing reports, data manipulation, and analysis.

  • Ability to travel within the U.S. and Canada up to 10% of time.

  • Ability to work non-standard business hours as needed to accommodate clients in different time zones.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Multi-lingual skills and multi-cultural or cross-cultural experience appreciated.

  • Experience with complex employee mediation.

  • Advanced understanding of HR concepts, processes, and services.

  • Experience developing and implementing HR policies, guidelines and procedures.

  • Experience successfully partnering with and influencing all levels of employees through effective communication skills, written and verbal, and high degree of emotional intelligence.

  • Ability to develop a working knowledge of relevant conservation issues.

  • Experience leading a team and effectively delivering HR services with multiple competing and time-sensitive priorities.

  • Experience developing and delivering presentations and training.

  • Advanced organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • Proven ability to work in a fast paced and highly visible environment.

Salary Information:

Canada

This position may only be based in a Canadian province/territory where TNC is registered (Ontario, Alberta, Northwest Territories). The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $165,000– $170,000 CAD for annual base salary. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is Canada. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate’s location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers competitive and comprehensive benefits packages tailored to the individual countries where we work. These may include health care benefits, retirement benefits, parental leave, paid time off, life insurance, and disability coverage as well as an employee assistance program and other life and well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Employees must submit their application by logging into Workday and applying via the Jobs Hub.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer.Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

jobs.description:
About Virtasant

Virtasant is a global technology services company with a network of over 4,000 technology professionals across 130+ countries. We specialize in cloud architecture, infrastructure, migration, and optimization, helping enterprises scale efficiently while maintaining cost control.

Our clients range from Fortune 500 companies to fast-growing startups, relying on us to build high-performance infrastructure, optimize cloud environments, and enable continuous delivery at scale.

About the role

A leading US healthcare workforce company has built an analytics and predictive proof of concept. Client reaction has been strong, and the platform is now moving to a full production build that will be taken to market. We are standing up a pod of five to six engineers to deliver it, working alongside the client’s product and business teams and training their internal engineers as we build. This is forward deployed work in the original sense: you embed with the client, you own an outcome, and you ship. Beyond the first build, the client plans to place small AI pods inside its business units, each pairing an FDE with an AI engineer and a software engineer, and each accountable for a measurable business result. Do the first engagement well and there is a long runway.

What You’ll Do

  • Act as the primary technical and consultative engineering lead.

  • Work directly with client stakeholders to understand business problems, workflows, constraints, and technical requirements.

  • Lead discovery sessions and technical workshops and translate business requirements into practical technical solutions.

  • Design and guide the data architecture using both PostgreSQL and Snowflake, including data modeling, data flows, and how the two systems integrate with the broader platform.

  • Design and evolve the architecture required to take an existing prototype into a secure, scalable, production-ready platform.

  • Make architectural decisions across backend services, APIs, data, integrations, infrastructure, security, and reliability.

  • Be hands-on in the implementation, including writing production-quality Python services and APIs when needed.

  • Work closely with platform, data, backend, and optimization engineers to establish a coherent technical direction.

  • Help define the roadmap from the existing prototype through MVP and production.

  • Identify technical risks, gaps, dependencies, and trade-offs and communicate them clearly to both technical and business stakeholders.

  • Partner with the client's existing architect and engineering team rather than operating as a separate vendor team.

  • Help establish engineering practices required for production, including observability, security, deployment, reliability, and maintainability.

  • Take ownership of outcomes and delivery rather than simply completing assigned tickets.

What We’re Looking For

This is an FDE-grade role. We are looking for someone who combines strong software engineering, architecture, consulting, and business context.

Must-Have Experience

  • 8+ years of experience in software engineering, solutions architecture, or a closely related technical discipline, with senior-level ownership of production systems.

  • Strong hands-on software engineering experience, particularly with Python and backend services/APIs.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills, with experience designing production-grade distributed systems.

  • Experience taking an existing prototype, proof of concept, or MVP and helping turn it into a production system.

  • Demonstrated experience working directly with clients or business stakeholders to discover requirements and shape technical solutions.

  • Experience leading technical discussions, workshops, design sessions, or architecture reviews with senior stakeholders.

  • Ability to translate business requirements and processes into technical architecture and implementation plans.

  • Strong understanding of production concerns including scalability, reliability, security, observability, deployment, and data architecture.

  • Ability to be both consultative and hands-on: you can discuss architecture with a CTO and then work with engineers to implement the solution.

  • Strong written and spoken English and the ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Comfortable working in a client-facing, ambiguous environment where requirements evolve as the product is built.


Nice-to-haves

  • Healthcare experience

  • HIPAA / PHI experience

  • Workforce management, staffing, or scheduling experience

  • Experience with HRIS, ERP, EMR/EHR, or scheduling-system integrations

  • Experience with Workday, UKG/Kronos, Oracle, or similar enterprise systems

  • Experience with optimization or ML systems

  • Experience with OR-Tools, Gurobi, OptaPlanner, XGBoost, or SciPy

  • Previous experience as a Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Architect, Solutions Engineer, or Staff Engineer in a client-facing environment

  • Experience transferring technical knowledge to client engineering teams through mentoring, pairing, workshops, or documentation

Our recruitment process

  • Recruiter interview (30 min)

  • Technical Interview (30 min)

  • Client Interview 1 (60 min)

We strive to move efficiently from step to step to make the recruitment process as fast as possible.

What we offer

Contract engagement through the Gigster network, full-time dedication expected.

Initial term aligned to the production build, with extension likely as the pod model expands across business units.

Compensation is competitive and set by experience and location


For this role, we can only consider candidates located in contiguous US states.
Also, we are only able to consider candidates who are either US citizens, or Green Card Holders, or sole proprietors of their own LLC company.
We are NOT able to consider candidates on any kind of visa that requires sponsorship, like STEM OPT, H4 EAD, F-1 OPT, L-2S, CPT, etc.

  • Source or select photography, and/or create simple graphics and short form video existing templates
  • Schedule posts across platforms and monitor basic engagement
  • Route content for review and approval per established workflows

The Medical Review Clinical Appeals Auditor(RN) is responsible for conducting Appeals reviews of new evidence presented by auditee’s, disputing all or part of the findings from medical review audit work completed by the medical review clinical audit team members, as well as communicate and support the identification of potential training opportunities or enhancements to training and/or concept review guideline materials and tools. Apollo's Rep Experience team builds the surface where sales teams do their actual work: prospecting, account and contact records, task management, dashboards, and the workflows that turn pipeline into revenue.   • You have the leadership skills to think and execute strategically but are not afraid to get your hands dirty when needed.
  • Your technical understanding of engineering systems, especially related to data, is second to none.

Skills and Relevant Experience

  • Understanding of data privacy and security fundamentals.

Great to Have

  • Familiarity with React, MongoDB, SQL and ElasticSearch.
  • Experience with data platforms such as Snowflake, Databricks, Airflow, and Looker.
  • Experience within Sales Tech..

Our Tech Stack

Our tech stack is React, Redux, and Next.js on the front end; Ruby, Python, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, and Redis on the backend; and Kubernetes, Docker, and Terraform for infrastructure.

The Senior Procurement Reporting Analyst (Senior Analyst, Labor Analytics & Workforce Data) will deliver data-driven insights and reporting across the company’s External Workforce to support strategic sourcing, workforce planning, financial management, and operational decision-making related to non-FTE labor. This role will perform advanced analytics, forecasting, modeling, and reporting; analyze external workforce spend, demand, utilization, and supplier performance; and translate complex workforce data into actionable insights. Working with Procurement, HR, Finance, Technology, and business stakeholders, the Senior Analyst will identify trends, risks, inefficiencies, and opportunities while contributing to continuous improvement in reporting, data quality, and workforce analytics capabilities.

What you will do:

  • Develop and maintain comprehensive reporting on external workforce spend, utilization, trends, and supplier performance.

  • Build and enhance dashboards, recurring reports, and analytical tools that support workforce and business decision-making.

  • Analyze workforce data to identify trends, patterns, risks, and opportunities requiring stakeholder attention.

  • Prepare executive-ready reporting and presentations that clearly communicate key findings and business implications.

  • Apply established metrics, KPIs, and reporting standards across external labor categories and recommend improvements to reporting methodologies, metrics, dashboards, and analytical processes.

  • Perform workforce demand forecasting, trend analysis, and capacity planning to support business and workforce planning.

  • Analyze workforce utilization, productivity, allocation, and demand across projects, departments, and business units.

  • Identify workforce gaps, inefficiencies, unusual trends, and optimization opportunities through quantitative analysis.

  • Develop scenarios and analytical models to help stakeholders evaluate workforce planning alternatives.

  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand workforce requirements and translate business questions into analytical solutions.

  • Apply established data standards, taxonomy, and governance requirements to external workforce reporting and analytics.

  • Monitor data accuracy, completeness, consistency, and integrity across workforce-related systems, including VMS, HRIS, procurement, and financial systems.

  • Research and resolve data discrepancies in partnership with system owners and business stakeholders.

  • Recommend enhancements to data definitions, controls, processes, and reporting standards.

  • Support technology teams with data requirements, testing, reporting enhancements, and analytics-related system improvements.

  • Document reporting methodologies, business rules, data definitions, and analytical processes.

  • Analyze external workforce cost drivers, rate trends, supplier performance, spending patterns, rate cards, pricing structures, workforce mix, and spend controls.

  • Conduct benchmarking and comparative analyses to identify potential cost savings and efficiency opportunities.

  • Support sourcing and supplier strategies through data-backed analysis and recommendations.

  • Measure and report on the financial and operational impact of workforce initiatives.

  • Partner with Procurement, Finance, HR, Technology, and business teams to provide workforce data and analytical support.

  • Translate complex data and analytical findings into clear, actionable insights for technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Prepare analyses and materials supporting business cases, leadership presentations, sourcing initiatives, and workforce planning activities.

  • Build productive working relationships across functions to understand business needs and improve the usefulness of workforce reporting.

  • Serve as a knowledge resource on external workforce data, reporting, and analytics, and provide analytical guidance and share best practices with less experienced team members as appropriate.

  • Support reporting and oversight related to external workforce governance and compliance requirements.

  • Monitor and report on non-FTE resources, including workforce populations with system or technology access.

  • Provide visibility into external workforce composition, including contractors, vendors, affiliated entities, regulators, and customer testers, as applicable.

  • Identify data quality or reporting issues that may create governance, financial, operational, or compliance risks.

  • Support adherence to organizational policies, data standards, controls, and applicable regulatory expectations.

  • Deliver accurate, timely, and actionable external workforce reporting and analysis that improves visibility into spend, demand, utilization, and supplier performance and supports workforce planning, sourcing, and cost-management decisions.

  • Identify meaningful trends, risks, inefficiencies, and optimization opportunities while improving reporting efficiency, data quality, and consistency through continuous process improvement.

What you will bring:

  • 4–7 years of experience in analytics, business intelligence, finance, workforce planning, procurement analytics, or a related discipline.

  • Experience working with external labor, contingent workforce, or related workforce data.

  • Demonstrated experience developing dashboards, analytical reporting, and data-driven insights.

  • Experience performing trend analysis, forecasting, financial analysis, or workforce modeling.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex data into clear insights and recommendations for business stakeholders.

  • Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.

  • Advanced proficiency with analytical and reporting tools such as Excel, SQL, Tableau, Power BI, or similar technologies.

  • Strong understanding of workforce metrics, spend analysis, financial concepts, and data visualization.

  • Ability to evaluate multiple data points and variables to identify trends, root causes, and potential solutions.

  • Ability to independently manage complex analytical assignments within established objectives and guidelines.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex information to non-technical audiences.

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy and integrity.

  • Ability to work effectively across functions and manage multiple priorities.

What will set you apart:

  • Experience in retirement services, financial services, or another highly regulated industry.

  • Familiarity with Vendor Management Systems (VMS), Managed Service Provider (MSP) models, HRIS, procurement systems, and financial systems.

Who We Are
DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers operate in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production.

Delivering DoiT Cloud Intelligence, the only solution that integrates advanced technology with human intelligence, we help our customers solve complex multicloud problems and drive efficiency.With decades of multicloud experience, we have specializations in Kubernetes, GenAI, CloudOps, and more. An award-winning strategic partner of AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, we work alongside more than 4,000 customers worldwide.

The Opportunity

Cloud spend is no longer just AWS, Google Cloud and Azure. Our customers now run a large and growing share of their technology spend through SaaS platforms, data clouds and AI vendors - and every one of those vendors is an integration that brings another slice of their spend into view.

You'll own DoiT's Integrations Framework and the experience built on top of it. This is a chance to define what a great integration experience looks like: a customer connects a new vendor in minutes, sees at a glance that their data is flowing, and handles credential rotation, reconnects and backfills themselves without thinking twice. On the framework side, you'll make adding the next vendor a small, well-understood piece of work rather than a project - so coverage grows as fast as the vendor landscape does.

You'll work AI-augmented from day one. Integration development is spec-driven work against constantly changing third-party APIs: one of the highest-leverage places to apply agentic AI tooling. We expect you to use it across your whole workflow and to have real opinions about where it earns its place.

Responsibilities

  • Building new integrations. This is the core of the role. Design and ship integrations against third-party billing and usage APIs - authentication, incremental sync, rate limits, error handling, schema drift - and invest in the Integrations Framework itself, along with testing harnesses and scaffolding, so the tenth integration takes a fraction of the effort of the first.
  • Working AI-augmented. Use AI daily across the full span of your work - exploring unfamiliar codebases and third-party APIs, prototyping approaches, generating and reviewing code, debugging, writing tests, and producing documentation. Push on what agentic tooling can do for this codebase, and bring judgement about where AI raises velocity and where a human still has to hold the quality bar.
  • Integration management experience. Build the interfaces customers use to connect, configure and trust their integrations: health and status visibility, actionable error states, credential and key rotation, and clear feedback when something needs attention.
  • Self-service by default. Design self-service into the framework from the start - backfills, reconnects and diagnostics that customers and internal teams run themselves.
  • API-first. Build capabilities so they're fully available through APIs, not just the UI. Both humans and agents should be able to drive the platform.
  • Implementing features end-to-end. From proposal, through spec and implementation, to maintenance. You're expected to propose things you think would be a good addition, not wait for a spec.

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, shipping and owning features in production
  • Strong TypeScript, including modern frontend work - React preferred
  • Hands-on experience with Go, or strong backend experience in another language (Python, Java, Node.js, C#) with genuine enthusiasm for ramping up in Go quickly
  • Real experience designing and consuming REST APIs, and integrating third-party APIs with all the mess that entails: auth flows, pagination, rate limits, partial failures, breaking changes
  • Comfortable across the stack. You may lean backend or lean frontend, but you can own a feature from the database through to the interface
  • Working proficiency in SQL
  • Experience developing solutions in the cloud and/or using cloud services (GCP, AWS or Azure)
  • A user-facing instinct for operational tooling - you care whether the error message actually tells someone what to do next
  • AI-augmented working style - you already use AI tools across your engineering workflow and can talk concretely about what you've got out of them
  • Strong knowledge of software engineering practices, design patterns and architectural principles
  • Demonstrated passion for creating high-quality web/SaaS apps
  • Excellent communication skills in English, both written and verbal
  • Self-organized, goal-oriented and self-motivated; confident, thorough and tenacious

  • Experience building integration platforms or extensibility frameworks as a core part of a product
  • Experience with cloud or SaaS billing data - AWS/GCP/Azure cost and usage exports, AI vendor billing data, marketplace billing, or the FOCUS specification
  • Experience with Google BigQuery, or with data pipelines and orchestration tooling (Dagster, Airflow)

PATH seeks a Consultant Clinical Research Associate with expertise in in vitro diagnostic (IVD) clinical validation studies. The consultant will provide operational and technical support to the planning, monitoring, execution, analysis, and dissemination of IVD validation studies conducted in diverse global settings, including low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Studies may include evaluations of rapid diagnostic tests, molecular assays, digital tools, and other emerging diagnostic technologies for priority epidemic and pandemic-prone pathogens, including the Bundibugyo virus.

The consultant will work closely with study investigators, laboratory partners, implementing organizations, regulatory experts, and country stakeholders to ensure studies are conducted in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), applicable regulatory requirements, and organizational standards.

Key responsibilities:

  • Support study design, planning, and implementation of IVD clinical performance validation studies.

  • Contribute to the development of study implementation plans, timelines, monitoring plans, and risk mitigation strategies. Assist with budget monitoring and resource planning for study activities.

  • Assist in preparation and review of study documents, including protocols, informed consent forms, case report forms, laboratory manuals, monitoring plans, and standard operating procedures as applicable.

  • Support ethics and regulatory submissions, amendments, and approvals.

  • Participate in site feasibility assessments, site selection, and study start-up activities.

  • Assist with development of training materials and facilitate investigator meetings.

  • Conduct routine study monitoring activities to ensure compliance with approved protocols, GCP, GCLP, sponsor and donor requirements, and applicable regulations.

  • Monitor enrollment, specimen collection, testing procedures, data quality, and study progress. Maintain accurate study documentation and tracking systems.

  • Review source documentation, case report forms, and study records for completeness, accuracy, and compliance.

  • Identify protocol deviations, quality issues, and operational risks and support corrective and preventive action plans.

  • Support study teams with issue resolution and implementation of quality improvement measures.

  • Provide technical guidance to study sites on study conduct, documentation, and reporting requirements.

  • Support study data review, query resolution, and data quality assurance activities.

  • Contribute to monitoring and evaluation of study metrics and performance indicators.

  • Assist in interpretation and communication of study findings. Support preparation of study reports, donor deliverables, and technical summaries.

  • Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, technical briefs, and policy-focused dissemination materials.

  • Support engagement with research stakeholders, including ministries of health, public health institutions, regulatory authorities, donors, and implementation partners.

Required qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in clinical research, public health, epidemiology, microbiology, laboratory medicine, biomedical sciences, or related discipline. A bachelor's degree with significant relevant experience may be considered.

  • Minimum 5 years of experience supporting clinical research studies involving investigational products (preferably IVDs).

  • Professional working proficiency in both French and English is required.

  • Demonstrated experience monitoring clinical studies in accordance with GCP and applicable quality standards.

  • Knowledge of clinical research operations, study monitoring, quality management systems, and regulatory requirements.

  • Experience with electronic data capture systems and clinical trial management systems.

  • Strong project management and organizational skills.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability and willingness to travel internationally, as required.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience working in outbreak response, global health, infectious diseases, public health surveillance, or pandemic preparedness programs.

  • Experience working with infectious disease diagnostics, including molecular, antigen, serology, or point-of-care testing platforms.

  • Experience supporting studies in Africa, Southeast Asia, Latin America, or other low- and middle-income geographies. Prior experience in the Democratic Republic of the Congo a plus.

  • Experience with diagnostic studies, especially for viral hemorrhagic fevers, antimicrobial resistance, emerging infectious diseases, respiratory pathogens, or other epidemic-prone pathogens.

  • Familiarity with diagnostic quality and regulatory frameworks.

  • Certification in clinical research (e.g., ACRP, SoCRA) preferred.

  • Experience supporting manuscript development and peer-reviewed publication processes.

    • building SuiteFlow automations in response to changing business needs;
    • managing the NetSuite integration ecosystem.

Knak is a mission-driven company
